key_insight: TideCache manages the different cache types in hybrid language models together, adapting GPU memory allocation as context length and request concurrency change. It combines transparent cache management with layer-wise streaming on CPU–GPU superchips.
problem_solved: Hybrid models mix global-attention layers and bounded-state layers with different cache requirements. Serving them efficiently requires balancing limited GPU memory across these caches and deciding which data stays on the GPU versus host memory.
method: Use a Transparent Cache Pool to redistribute physical memory pages among cache components while preserving fixed virtual addresses.
Coordinate cache residency across GPU and host memory on CPU–GPU superchips.
Use layer-wise streaming, as indicated by the title; the supplied abstract is truncated and does not describe its implementation or all three system components.
impact: The approach targets more efficient serving of hybrid language models under changing workloads. The supplied excerpt does not include performance results, so throughput, latency, and memory savings cannot be quantified.

Conceptual workload panel showing how context length and concurrent requests change cache demand.
paper_title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
paper_authors: Jinbin Luo, Xiaozhe Yao, Shang Yang, Zhijian Liu, Song Han
